data.title: Redox activation of ATG5 licenses autophagy upon nutrient restriction
data.authors: Shin S; Korobkina ED; Lennicke C; Burger N; Zhang B; Xiao H; Wang Y; Petrocelli JJ; Wei SM; Wood D; Lei Y; Zhang X; Perez-Matos MC; Sharif MA; Zhang J; Cochemé HM; Mair WB; Chouchani ET

evidence.label: Preprint, not peer-reviewed
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human cell lines and mice; tissue-resolved cysteine redox proteomics (OxiDR atlas) under dietary restriction
data.finding: Dietary restriction selectively oxidizes a specific, tissue-resolved set of cysteines rather than oxidizing the proteome broadly. One of the most strongly oxidized is Cys19 on the core autophagy protein ATG5; this oxidation is required for ATG5 to bind ATG10 and form the ATG5-ATG12 conjugate that lipidates LC3B and builds the autophagosome. In mice lacking this redox switch, nutrient restriction fails to trigger autophagy, causing severe tissue pathology and early death -- a single oxidized cysteine gates the autophagic response to fasting.
data.abstract_excerpt: Dietary restriction (DR) protects against metabolic disease, extends lifespan, and is associated with remodeling of tissue reactive oxygen species (ROS). ROS control biological adaptation through reversible oxidation of protein cysteines, yet the targets of DR-initiated redox signaling are unknown. Here we generate OxiDR, a tissue-resolved atlas of the cysteine redox proteome that quantifies oxidation state under DR.

extracted_findings.intervention: Dietary restriction; ATG5 Cys19 redox-dead mutation
extracted_findings.effect: Oxidation of ATG5 Cys19 was required for nutrient-restriction-induced autophagy; mice lacking it developed tissue pathology and early death.
